articles.title: Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings Beats Q3 Forecast and Raises 2026 Outlook
articles.summary: NCLH's third quarter came in better than expected, so it lifted its full-year guidance.
articles.recap: Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings said its July to September results topped its own guidance. Strong last-minute bookings and higher onboard spending helped, along with tighter cost control. The company raised its full-year 2026 outlook and expects net yields to grow 1% to 2% in 2027. Bookings for the year ahead have improved a bit but are still below where it wants them, and it is counting on Great Stirrup Cay's new waterpark and better marketing to help.

articles.title: Villa Vie Plans Chapter 11 After Odyssey Residents Sent Ashore in Cambodia
articles.summary: The residential cruise company says it will file for bankruptcy after halting its ship.
articles.recap: Villa Vie Residences plans to file for Chapter 11 after stopping operations of the Villa Vie Odyssey. More than 200 residents, mostly Americans, were taken ashore in Sihanoukville, Cambodia. The CEO blamed fuel prices that jumped from about $700 a ton to $2,000 to $3,000 a ton this year. Some residents dispute the company's claim that it is covering their hotel stays.

articles.title: MSC Opera Sailing Cancelled by Text One Day Before Departure
articles.summary: Guests got last-minute texts saying their MSC Opera cruise was off for technical reasons.
articles.recap: MSC Opera was due to leave Civitavecchia, Italy on October 29, but guests were told by text the day before that the cruise was cancelled. The ship has been in dry dock in Malta this month, and MSC hasn't said exactly what went wrong. Some guests first thought the texts were a scam. The notice promises a full refund plus travel and hotel costs, while some guests say they were moved to a later start from Livorno instead.

articles.title: Viking Takes Delivery of New River Ship Viking Haki
articles.summary: Viking's newest 190-guest Longship is joining its Rhine, Main and Danube fleet.
articles.recap: Viking has taken delivery of the Viking Haki, a 190-guest Longship with 95 staterooms. The ship was recently named in Amsterdam. It will sail routes like Rhine Getaway, Grand European Tour and Christmas Market trips. Viking expects 17 more river ships by 2028, which would bring its river fleet to 114.

articles.title: Barcelona Port Protest Disrupts About 13,000 Cruise Guests
articles.summary: Port workers blocked Barcelona's cruise terminals, leaving guests to walk in and out.
articles.recap: Port workers protesting a bonus dispute blocked road access to Barcelona's cruise terminals on October 28. Four ships were in port: Odyssey of the Seas, Mein Schiff 7, AIDAmar and Norwegian Escape. No ships were in danger, but vehicles couldn't reach the terminals, so many guests walked up to about two miles each way. More protests and strikes are possible in Spain ahead of its November 29 elections.

articles.title: SS United States to Become World's Largest Artificial Reef on Nov. 12
articles.summary: The famous 1952 ocean liner will be sunk off Destin, Florida next month.
articles.recap: Okaloosa County says the SS United States will be sunk on November 12, 2026, about 22 nautical miles southwest of Destin-Fort Walton Beach. Once on the seabed, it will be the largest artificial reef in the world. A sendoff ceremony is planned for November 11, and a live viewing party will show the sinking on a big screen. The county bought the liner in 2024 and cleaned it up environmentally before the sinking.

articles.title: Port Everglades Wins $30.75 Million Federal Grant
articles.summary: Fort Lauderdale's port gets federal money to widen a fuel slip for bigger tankers.
articles.recap: Port Everglades received $30.75 million from the federal Port Infrastructure Development Program. The money will help move a bulkhead and widen Slip 1 to 450 feet so larger fuel tankers can dock. The full project is expected to cost $184.5 million, with construction starting in 2028. Port Everglades is one of the three busiest cruise homeports in the world.

articles.title: Carnival Reveals Farewell Voyages as Two Ships Leave Australia
articles.summary: Carnival Adventure and Carnival Luminosa will say goodbye to Australia in March 2028.
articles.recap: Carnival announced the last Australian voyages for Carnival Adventure and Carnival Luminosa, which leave the market in March 2028. Adventure will sail from Sydney to Tokyo, then a round trip from Tokyo, then across the Pacific to Seattle. Luminosa will make a 23-day trip from Sydney to Los Angeles by way of French Polynesia and Hawaii. Both ships keep sailing their regular Australian trips until then.
